subject: SKU packaging & PO IDs — impact on discount eligibility and net terms
messages:
From: Lena Torres <ltorres@healthexample.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Carlos Mendoza <c.mendoza@erpservices.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question: PO line items + packaging type affecting discounts?

Hi Rishi,

Hope you're well. Procurement here at HealthCo is finalizing the PO but we've hit a small snag with how our ERP emits line items. We have two packaging approaches in our catalog: (A) "Seat-based" SKUs for named-user deployments and (B) "Token-pack" SKUs for our usage lanes. Our finance team is concerned that because our PO will include both packaging types across multiple cost centers, that might disqualify us from the volume discount slabs we agreed in the quote.

Couple quick questions:
- Do Redwood discount slabs evaluate at the PO level or at the billing-entity/commit level?
- Does the presence of multiple SKU packaging styles on a single PO break automatic discounting?
- We typically require net45 payment terms; does that affect discount eligibility versus net30?

I've attached an export from our ERP and a sample PO (HealthCo_sample_PO_v1.pdf) so you can see how fields are emitted. Can you advise what we should change on our side to ensure the invoice mapping preserves the discount?

Thanks — Lena
Procurement Director, HealthCo
attachments: HealthCo_sample_PO_v1.pdf (pdf), ERP_export_lines.csv (csv)

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Lena Torres <ltorres@healthexample.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question: PO line items + packaging type affecting discounts?

Hi Lena — thanks for the context and the sample PO, that helps. Short answers up front:

- Discount slabs at Redwood are evaluated against the committed billing entity (account level / deal) not strictly per individual PO file. However, we require PO metadata (PO ID, billing entity, and SKU code) to map invoice lines back to the same commit for automation.
- Multiple packaging styles on a single PO do not automatically void a discount, but they do complicate ERP mapping. If different packaging maps to different internal SKUs that are treated as separate pricing buckets, our billing automation will split them and apply slab math per resulting bucket unless the PO contains a single commit reference (our "commit_id" field in the PO) that ties everything to the same commercial commitment.
- Net terms (net30 vs net45) do not change the slab calculation itself, but extended payment terms can affect eligibility for promotional/early-payment discounts. The negotiated contract clause for this deal will govern any exceptions.

Action items I recommend now:
1) Add a single commit reference in the PO lines (a short string) — we can accept it as PO custom field "commit_id" or put it in PO line memo. This lets our billing unify multiple SKUs under the same discount bucket.
2) Ensure each PO line includes the Redwood SKU code (we've attached a small PO template, Redwood_PO_template_for-SKUs.csv).
3) If HealthCo needs net45 formally, please flag it so we can route an exception request to Finance. That exception won't change slab math but is used by our billing & collections teams.

I'll let Vanessa jump in on invoice cadence implication (monthly vs weekly statements) and Marissa can advise on how we handle legacy ERP exports.

—Rishi
Sr. Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
attachments: Redwood_PO_template_for-SKUs.csv (csv)

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Lena Torres <ltorres@healthexample.com>, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 08:47:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question: PO line items + packaging type affecting discounts? — invoice cadence notes

Lena — quick operational note from Billing:

- Invoice cadence matters for how discounts appear on statements. Our platform can issue weekly or monthly invoices, but for discount slab recognition we prefer a monthly consolidated statement per commit_id. If your ERP pushes weekly POs that are split across cost centers, we will still aggregate them only if they contain the same commit_id AND bill-to entity.
- For ERPs that cannot emit a custom field, the common workaround is to use a standard PO prefix (e.g., HC-DEAL9843-) in every PO ID so the string match ties POs together. That works for a lot of legacy systems.
- If you need health-care-specific accounting (multiple cost centers mapped to a single legal entity), we can provide a one-off mapping table during onboarding; Marissa, can you confirm the lead time?

Also, a head's up: promotional tiers (first-year onboarding discounts) require the invoice to be issued within calendar-month buckets we recognize. If you stagger invoices across months, some of that promotional volume might fall into the next bucket and reduce the effective discount.

—Vanessa Ortiz
Billing Ops, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Lena Torres <ltorres@healthexample.com>, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 14:52:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Question: PO line items + packaging type affecting discounts? — ERP mapping and exceptions

Hi all — adding the ERP perspective. Carlos (copied) helped implement similar mapping for another healthcare customer last quarter. Practical notes:

- If HealthCo's ERP can export a simple CSV nightly with: PO_ID, PO_LINE, SKU_CODE, AMOUNT, BILL_TO_ENTITY, COST_CENTER, COMMIT_ID (optional) — we can ingest it and guarantee correct slab attribution. If COMMIT_ID is not possible, use the PO_ID prefix approach Vanessa suggested.
- We can accept split invoices for milestone billing but discount computation is done on the aggregated recognized revenue per month per commit. That means smaller, scattered invoices can push you below a threshold temporarily.
- If HealthCo needs net45, please have Procurement raise a formal exception. I've attached our discount-exception-request-form.docx — Finance needs the requested term, justification, and the AR contact. Exception requests typically take 3–5 business days.

Carlos — can you confirm the CSV sample and whether the mapping team will need additional fields for your ERP connector?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Onboarding, Redwood Inference
attachments: discount-exception-request-form.docx
